risks: Static review only: supplied hashes, checkpoint contents, environment, scheduler implementation, transport dependency and reported test execution were not independently authenticated. Execution eligibility depends on the specified live provenance gates succeeding.

Autograd checks scalar sums, not individual class derivatives. Per-entry one-sided finite differences provide complementary coverage, but retain truncation and cancellation error. Any frozen-tolerance failure must terminate without numerical rescue.

Projector and analytic-log formulas assume exactly normalized states. The implementation permits small norm errors; recorded geometry residuals and actual native-logit comparison are necessary numerical qualifications, not exact floating-point identities.

The CE cross-gap identity is constructed from the same analytic response terms and is not an independent numerical check by itself. Separate full and pinched autograd and finite-difference CE checks provide the substantive implementation checks.

The 900-second timeout and 8192-MB allocation are prospective bounds, not demonstrated runtime sufficiency. Parent fixtures replace scientific execution and initial guards; they do not establish numerical canary success or real-data completion.

R96 evaluation uses batch size 32 while this replay uses 4. Exact prediction-derived metrics and tightly bounded CE agreement may fail from numerical differences; such failure must remain a stopped diagnostic, not justify changing tolerances or replaying.

Source revision and execution-contract authenticity rely partly on the external admission gate and scheduler receipt; response_job.checked does not independently verify the repository revision or a separately pinned execution-contract digest.

Persistent registration retains earlier recipes, including training recipes. This review admits only the single frozen response-analysis submission and does not authorize executing those retained recipes.
Reused development data and separately trained eta-zero baselines cannot establish independent benefit, training causality, finite-eta improvement or substantive novelty.

theory_mapping.summary: The supplied EPS is 1e-6. The rank-one P/Q coefficients, logarithmic mean and factor-two cross-block contribution match equations 1–2 under normalized-state assumptions.
The source pinches A/N after computing the full-A scale and retains the original utility readout. decomposition uses that same scale and denominator, matching equation 3.
H is implemented as the labeled response minus its eta-zero softmax-weighted average. Expected CE derivatives are -H; full-minus-pinched equals the negative cross advantage.

Each call reconstructs the same eta-independent generator from fixed states and matched utilities. Scalar eta remains in the matrix-exponential computation graph. The three-point forward formula checks the derivative without negative-eta calls.

The fixed helpful/harmful labels test opposite CE responses. Orthogonal Q tokens with utilities +1/-1 yield diagonal response 1/sqrt(3) and zero cross response. Constant utilities yield zero response. These fixtures precede real-data analysis.

The legacy overlap-plus-EPS attention agrees algebraically with eta zero for unit states. The analysis additionally compares actual legacy logits and separately invokes each model's deployed forward, including the distinct simplex tilt.

The execution path restores strict state dictionaries, freezes parameters, performs eta-only differentiation, and checks state fingerprints and checkpoint hashes. It invokes no optimizer, training loop, checkpoint save or cloud operation.

The supplied controls specify one non-replayable scheduler attempt, synchronous child execution, failure evidence retention, completion-marker-last publication, idle-only paired configuration updates and exact rollback. R97 math approval is correctly distinguished from this bounded execution review; L5 remains unaccepted.
